_doc: The exception register: known, deliberate deviations that a tier would
`qa exceptions` fails the build if an entry is past its expiry or is
missing a reason, owner or expiry. A suppression that has outlived its
reason is itself a defect — it hides a real failure and nobody is looking
at it any more. Renew deliberately or fix the underlying issue.
Keep `match` as narrow as the thing being suppressed: `selContains` is
there so one exception does not silence a whole page.
`match.source: "design-reconciliation"` marks an entry that belongs to the
ONE-TIME comparison against the designer's reference implementation
(design-diff.mjs, retired and removed after the one-time run): a deviation from the design that we
decided to keep. Those entries are read ONLY by that tool.
qa/conformance/structure.qa.mjs skips every entry carrying a `source`,
because a rule like `table-columns` scoped to /due-dates would otherwise
silence a genuine future column drop on exactly the page whose dropped
Action column is the reason that tier exists.
Design questions and architectural findings do NOT go here — they go in
pulse-backend/docs/qa/findings.md, which tracks them to a resolution.

exceptions.reason: PatentWorldMap is a pan/zoom surface with zoom-in, zoom-out and expand controls. Its canvas (1125px) is deliberately wider than the 750px frame and clipped; panning is how you reach the rest. Verified by screenshot 2026-08-29 — the map renders correctly and all continents are reachable.

Same element as world-map-pannable-canvas. The clipped-text rule counts the card's own text because the map card has a single child wrapper; the text itself (title, subtitle, legend) is fully visible — it is the map canvas below it that extends past the frame.

The copilot trio (analyze-document, draft-field, generate-summary) plus the multipart upload-idea-file path and update-requested-change are 501 BY DESIGN until agent support exists — CLAUDE.md 'Known-not-built'. They are deliberately unmapped so the failure is named rather than silent. Listed explicitly so a SIXTH unmapped call fails the check instead of hiding among them.

The dashboard's awaiting-action list renders each idea as a leaf <button> whose accessible name IS the idea title plus its age ('Temporal Score-Delta Monitoring Harness awaiting 6d'). Four leaf buttons in a row are indistinguishable by shape from a toolbar, so the repeated-block detector cannot anonymise them without also anonymising Sort/Columns/Export. Every idea created on demo would otherwise move the baseline. The list's PRESENCE is still asserted — only the per-idea names are suppressed. Covers both directions of the signature-set diff, which is why no rule is pinned; the substring is specific to these cards.

ReviewQueueWorkspace (LEGAL_COUNSEL and TECH_COMMITTEE only) titles the disclosure it currently has open in an h2, and which disclosure is first in the queue is data. No other role renders an h2 on /ideas, so this cannot silence anything else. The queue's own cards are already anonymised by the repeated-card detector; this is the single selected record.

Same element as review-queue-names-the-open-disclosure: the 'Open full record for <title>' link names the selected disclosure. The link's presence is asserted by the journey tier, which clicks it; only the data-derived name is suppressed here.

ACCEPTED design deviation. The reference (pulse-design-auto @3f9b2fdb) has one 'Settings' nav item pointing at /workspace, which held both administration and a 'Your profile' tab. The saurrx#2 IA split (our commit 135e275) made /workspace administration-only and gave every other role a standalone /profile, so 'Settings' became 'Workspace' (photon admin, counsel) or 'Profile' (everyone else). This is the newer design, not drift.

ACCEPTED design deviation. Same IA split as design-profile-left-the-workspace: the reference's tablist (People / Manage access / Your profile) is gone. /workspace is now a client identity card whose 'Edit workspace' opens OrganizationDetails in a dialog, with People beneath; the 'Your profile' tab's content lives at /profile, where 'Edit profile' is still offered. Recorded in CLAUDE.md §5.

ACCEPTED design deviation, and a deliberate one: commit 135e275 records that the saurrx#2 merge appended the design's mock-data columns while dropping ours, leaving renderer cases with no matching column. We keep Title / Days / Action / Last updated and drop the reference's 'Family members' (every mock row reads N/A; the API exposes no such field) and 'Current event' (in the reference it duplicates the Event column verbatim). The Action column is the one this whole tier exists to protect — it is present, and the baseline now pins it.

ACCEPTED design deviation: /patents carries a PRN column the reference does not, from the per-client idea reference prefix that landed with the saurrx#2 port (CLAUDE.md §12). An added column, not a dropped one.

ACCEPTED design deviation, vocabulary only. The reference says 'My disclosures' / 'New disclosure' to the inventor; this product says 'My ideas' / 'Submit an idea', consistently across nav, page heading and empty state. Both are internally consistent; ours matches the rest of the product (the /ideas route, the Ideas nav item photon roles see, the idea/ API).

ACCEPTED design deviation. The reference styles zoom-in / zoom-out / expand as three separate translucent pills (p-2, rounded-lg, bg-zinc-200/50); ours renders one bordered segmented group of 36px cells. Landed deliberately with the saurrx#2 port (commit 135e275) and is consistent with the segmented controls elsewhere in this app. Same three controls, same order, same labels — only the chrome differs.

ACCEPTED, and not a product decision at all: sonner names its live region 'Notifications (F8)' in the reference's version and 'Notifications alt+T' in ours. A dependency's hotkey hint, not a design difference.

ACCEPTED design deviation, in our favour. The reference's counsel workspace is a profile card; ours is a real members table (Team member / Email / Role / Status / Action) with Invite administrator and Generate inventor link. Built beyond the design against real endpoints — CLAUDE.md §12 'people/roles/suspend'.

DashboardStats renders the '<n>+ pending actions - Review all' button only when the awaiting-action list has MORE rows than fit (hiddenCount > 0, DashboardStats.tsx:598). Whether it exists is therefore a property of how many ideas are awaiting a decision on demo that day, not of the page's structure, and it flapped in and out of the baseline as ideas were submitted and reviewed. The card ITSELF is still asserted; only this overflow affordance is suppressed. Recording it either way would bake a data state into a structural baseline.
